solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dish: take hearts of some eels, feta and stew

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its inside, so each of the next four words gives up all but its outer letters

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: pick the best bits of eels and feta and stew them together.
explanation.walkthrough: The middles are OM, EL, ET and TE, run together in order. 'stew' looks like a cooking verb but is just the last word to be cored.
explanation.definitionFit: An omelette is a cooked egg dish, so it is one example of a dish.

clue.text: What can run on green power, after replacing lead

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter, which is swapped here for another

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what machine might be driven on eco-friendly 'green power'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green power' reads as renewable energy, but 'green' belongs to the definition: a lawn. Swapping the first letter of POWER (P) for M gives the machine; the clue does not say which letter comes in, so the definition decides it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawnmower is pushed or driven across grass, and a bowling or putting green is grass.

clue.text: Song to perform without piano

indicators.note: without means the following letter is taken away from the word before

parts.note: to play is to perform, as on a stage or instrument
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A singer is told to sing unaccompanied, with no piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A lay is an old word for a short narrative poem or ballad meant to be sung.

clue.text: Bone that is broken in accident, first of all

indicators.note: first of all means the first letter of every one of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: A doctor's remark about which bone snapped in a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two bones of the lower leg.

clue.text: Wandering rodent getting in damaged rice

indicators.note: getting in means the rodent goes inside the scrambled rice
damaged means the letters of rice are spoilt and rearranged

parts.note: a rat is a rodent

explanation.surface: A stray rat has got into a sack of spoilt rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wandering rodent' reads as one stray animal, but 'Wandering' alone is the definition; 'damaged' scrambles the rice to ERIC before 'getting in' does its work.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular or unpredictable, straying from a fixed course, as a wandering mind does.

clue.text: Brawl's beginning after pub remark that's hurtful

indicators.note: after means the brawl's first letter comes behind the pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: beginning means only the first letter of brawl is used

explanation.surface: A fight in a pub starts with a cutting insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a pointed, wounding comment, like the hooked point of an arrow.

clue.text: French restaurant chain mostly needs supporters up front

indicators.note: up front means the supporters come first, ahead of the shortened chain

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a series is a chain of events or things

explanation.surface: A French restaurant chain mostly needs backers to invest at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French restaurant chain' reads as one phrase, but the definition ends at 'restaurant'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brasserie is an informal French-style eatery serving food and beer.

clue.text: What get-out clause may do regarding rental agreement

parts.note: re means regarding, as in a letter heading
a lease is a contract to rent property

explanation.surface: A tenant asks what an escape clause in a rental contract allows.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-out clause frees a party from an obligation, letting them off the contract.

clue.text: Son has method to persuade

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: A son has his own technique for winning people round.
explanation.definitionFit: To sway someone is to influence their opinion and bring them round.

clue.text: Crustacean is lean crab, minced

indicators.note: minced means chopped up finely, so the letters are cut up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A seafood note: this crustacean is a lean crab, chopped fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnacles are marine crustaceans that cling to rocks and ship hulls.

clue.text: Lengthen professional treatise

parts.note: a pro is a professional
a tract is a short treatise or pamphlet

explanation.surface: An expert's lengthy treatise is asked to be extended further.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract something is to draw it out or prolong it in time.

clue.text: Strange Argentine fruit

indicators.note: strange means the letters of the next word are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd-looking fruit from Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit like a mandarin orange.

clue.text: Returning friend's bad make-up

indicators.note: returning means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: pals are friends, and the friend's gives the plural form

explanation.surface: A friend comes back with badly applied cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friend's' gives PALS, which reads backwards. Slap is theatrical or informal British slang for make-up, especially heavily applied.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap is British slang for cosmetics, usually thick or garishly applied face paint.

clue.text: Pelted with rocks, who's ending in dents all over?

indicators.note: all over means the letters are scattered about and rearranged
ending means only the last letter of who is used

explanation.surface: Someone pelted with rocks wonders whose dents cover them all over.
explanation.walkthrough: The O ending 'who' goes in with DENTS, and 'all over' shuffles the six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To stone someone is to throw rocks at them, so being stoned is being pelted that way.

clue.text: Trial about old play such as King Lear

indicators.note: about means the trial goes round the old, wrapping it

parts.note: a try is an attempt or trial
aged means old

explanation.surface: An old play like King Lear is put on trial.
explanation.definitionFit: King Lear is one of Shakespeare's great tragedies, a drama ending in catastrophe.

clue.text: Noble and key united game

parts.note: D is a musical key
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: An aristocrat and a key united player in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A duchess is a woman of high noble rank, wife of a duke or holding the title herself.

clue.text: Instrument that's for holding ice cream

definitions.meaning: a brass instrument like a small trumpet
the British word for an ice-cream cone

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that doubles as an ice-cream holder.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an ice-cream cone is also called by this name, from the same horn shape as the brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The brass horn and the wafer cone both take their name from a horn shape.

clue.text: Unavoidable death of obese European

parts.note: fat means obese

explanation.surface: An overweight European meets an inevitable demise.
explanation.definitionFit: One's destiny, especially an inescapable end such as dying, is called one's lot or doom.

clue.text: Supervisor carrying tea for each one shortly

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
per means for each, as in per person

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as the word itself before cutting

explanation.surface: A supervisor carries cups of tea, one for each person.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperon is an older person who accompanies and oversees young people, a minder or escort.

clue.text: What's needed for mass change, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, a sound-alike

parts.note: to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A question about what a large-scale change requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass' looks like 'large-scale', but it is the church service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catholic Mass is celebrated at the communion table in a church.

clue.text: OAP perhaps is bold going topless, I note

indicators.note: going topless means the word loses its first letter, its top in a down clue

parts.note: E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A pensioner is bold enough to go topless, says a note.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP is British for old-age pensioner.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal word for an elderly person, of whom a pensioner is an example.

clue.text: King meeting unruly body of soldiers

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A king meets a disorderly troop of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment is a permanent military unit, a large body of troops.

clue.text: Bird's repeated note

indicators.note: repeated means the note is given twice over

parts.note: do (doh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A bird's call is a single note sung over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: The dodo is an extinct flightless bird of Mauritius.

clue.text: River delta round top of Nile

parts.note: D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet
O is round in shape

indicators.note: top of means the first letter, the top in a down clue

explanation.surface: The Nile's delta lies around the river's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delta' and 'Nile' suggest a river picture, but neither is the definition's river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Don is a major river in Russia, and others flow in England and Scotland.

clue.text: Sort you'll find in shanty, perhaps

indicators.note: you'll find in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sea shanty might be one kind of song you would come across.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort is a kind or category, as in 'that sort of thing'.

clue.text: Contracted second hospital to manage most of Kent

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Kent is a county in south-east England

explanation.surface: A second hospital is hired to run most of the county of Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracted' looks like 'hired under contract', but means made smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrunken means reduced in size, made smaller, as a contracted muscle is.
